column1: # Black-Box Testing Findings — PyTodo Pro Web UI

Manual black-box functional testing was conducted on the PyTodo Pro Web UI (`http://127.0.0.1:5000/`) using Google Chrome on Windows 11 with a clean SQLite database (`pytodo_pro.db`). Testing was executed from an end-user perspective across all nine user-facing web requirements (`REQ-01` through `REQ-09`) using four black-box test design techniques: Equivalence Partitioning (EP)
column4: and State Transition Testing. A total of 28 test cases (`TC-BB-001` through `TC-BB-028`) were executed using the baseline test account `ayamgoreng` (password `akusukaayam`)
column5: resulting in 23 passed test cases (82.14%) and 5 failed test cases (17.86%) that exposed 5 confirmed defects (`DEF-001` through `DEF-005`).

column1: ### Finding 1: Unhandled Server Crash (`ValueError`) on Non-Standard Year Formats (`DEF-001`)
During Equivalence Partitioning testing of the Create Task (`/tasks/new`) and Edit Task (`/tasks/<id>/edit`) workflows
column2: submitting a valid task title and category alongside a five-digit year in the due date field (`19999-06-14`) caused the Flask web server to crash completely with an unhandled Python `ValueError` traceback page (`ValueError: time data '19999-06-14' does not match format '%Y-%m-%d'`). Instead of validating the input safely and returning an inline form error message
column3: the application exposed its internal backend stack trace to the browser (`screenshots/bug 1_date error.png`). Furthermore
column4: once this crash occurred
column5: the web application's normal return navigation stopped functioning properly until the user manually reloaded a valid route.

column1: ### Finding 3: Duplicate Account Registration Overwrites Existing User Records (`DEF-003`)
When testing invalid equivalence partitions on the User Registration page (`/register`)
column2: re-submitting an already registered username (`ayamgoreng`) with the same password (`akusukaayam`) was permitted by the system rather than being rejected with a duplicate-account warning (`screenshots/register.png`). Completing this duplicate registration silently overwrote the existing user record and wiped out all previously saved tasks belonging to `ayamgoreng`
column3: representing a critical data-loss vulnerability in account management.

column1: ### Finding 4: Multi-Account Registration Blocked Within the Same Browser Session (`DEF-004`)

Rather than allowing multiple independent users to register separate accounts on the same browser
column4: the application enforced an unintended one-browser-one-account restriction.

column1: ### Finding 5: Lack of Password Complexity Enforcement During Registration (`DEF-005`)

While boundary testing on `/register` confirmed that the application strictly enforces minimum and maximum character lengths—rejecting two-character usernames like `us` with `"Username must be 3-20 characters (letters
column3: underscore)."` and rejecting passwords shorter than eight characters with `"Password must be at least 8 characters."` (`screenshots/register_username_password_error.png` and `screenshots/register_password_error.png`)—the password field accepts purely lowercase alphabetic strings such as `akusukaayam` without requiring numbers

column5: or special symbols. Because length is the sole validation rule applied
column6: users can register accounts with weak
column7: easily guessed passwords.
